conventions.purpose: Names and jargon the written-form stage must not rewrite. A written-form span (number, money, time, unit, year...) that overlaps a protected term keeps its spoken words. MODEL spans are exempt unless the entry sets blocks_models, so the AI lexicon in models.json keeps working.
conventions.spoken: Lowercase recognizer word sequences, at most 4 words. Hyphens split words and outer punctuation is ignored, so 'eleven labs' also matches 'Eleven-Labs,'. List digit forms too (e.g. '11 labs'); a digit form also catches text the stage has already converted, which then renders canonically (COVID 19 -> COVID-19).
conventions.written: The canonical spelling. It replaces a match only when the letters and digits are identical apart from case, spacing and joining marks (- . & + '), so 'Eleven Labs' -> 'ElevenLabs' but 'Seven Eleven' never becomes '7-Eleven'. Otherwise the spoken words stay.
conventions.case: Cue required before the entry applies. 'name' (default): every word other than and/of/the/to/in/on/for/a/an/at/by starts with a capital, as recognizers write names; a one-word spoken form equal to the written form applies in any case. 'lower': the match has no capitals (jargon that a capitalized lexicon name would otherwise claim). 'any': no cue.
conventions.blocks_models: Optional; also blocks a MODEL span that consists only of the term (jargon the AI lexicon lists as a mishearing). Longer anchored names such as 'GPT five codec' or 'codecs CLI' still render.
conventions.user_overrides: Enabled Vocabulary entries win: their heard and written phrases are already protected from written form, and a shipped term never re-spells text inside one. A Vocabulary written form without spaces also respells its split spoken form ('Tail Scale' -> 'Tailscale').
conventions.maintenance: Add an entry only for a demonstrated misfire or a name recognizers routinely split; give the reason in 'why'. Keep rewrite/evaluation/.cache/written-form-2026-10/lexicon/terms.json identical (wf_render.py reads it).

terms.why: Voice AI company. In a reviewed dictation 'Eleven Labs V four' became '11 Labs V4'.
Video AI company; 'Twelve Labs' became '12 Labs' under both rules and v3.
AI inference host; 'Base Ten' became 'Base 10'. Lowercase 'base ten' (the number base) still becomes 'base 10'.
Tech company (Hunyuan models); 'Ten Cent' parsed as money: '10 cent'.
'at Seven Eleven' parses as the time 7:11. Spoken words stay; recognizer digits render 7-Eleven. Lowercase 'at seven eleven' is still a time.
'Thirty Seven Signals' is written '37 Signals' by the number rules; the digit form then renders 37signals.
'Twenty Three and Me' becomes '23 and Me'; the digit form then renders 23andMe. Lowercase '23 and me' is ordinary prose.
The unit rule writes digits before 'inch' at any value: '9 Inch Nails'.
'COVID nineteen' becomes 'COVID 19'; the digit form renders the standard COVID-19.
The magnitude rule writes 'Y two K' as 'Y 2K'; the digit form renders Y2K.
Idiom: v3 labels 'twenty twenty' a year and writes 'hindsight is 2020'. Kept as spoken words.
Audio/video codecs. The AI lexicon repairs 'codecs' to Codex; a reviewed dictation 'some newer codecs' became 'newer Codex'. Capitalized 'Codecs', 'codecs CLI' and 'GPT five codec' still render.
Singular of codecs; same lexicon collision.
This app; recognizers split it into two words.
Sister product from the same studio; recognizers split it.
Networking product; split in a reviewed dictation ('Tail Scale').
Routinely split by recognizers; 'Three' must stay a word.
